summary: Journal perf fix VERIFIED end-to-end on mobile viewport 390x844. Root behavior confirmed: save/delete now update local state only — no GET /api/trades refetch after any mutation. Detailed evidence per phase (network counters captured via page.on('request')): (1) CREATE — created 5 consecutive trades (win 100 / loss 50 / win 200 / loss 30 / win 75). Result: 5 POST /api/trades, 0 GET /api/trades. Modal open→close latency was tight and consistent: 0.89/0.90/0.86/0.90/0.88s (avg 0.89s ≈ pure network RTT of POST). New cards appeared at the TOP of the list immediately after each save — verified by reading DOM testIDs after each save. No lag, no freeze, no modal-stuck state across 5 sequential creates. (2) EDIT — edited the top card (pnl 100 → 999). Result: 1 PATCH, 0 GET. Card innerText after save: 'XAUUSD · Compra\n2026-09-27 · Ganada\n+999.00 USD ...'. Update rendered in-place without refetch (setTrades map on updated.id). Edit latency 0.40s. (3) DELETE — clicked delete on the 2nd card. DOM element trade-<id> was gone within 148ms of click (before backend responded), confirming optimistic filter-out. Backend then completed with 1 DELETE, 0 GET afterwards. Fallback (setTrades(await getTrades(...))) was NOT triggered because DELETE succeeded. (4) REGRESSION account isolation — initial Journal load fired GET /api/trades?account_id=32c282d6-071c-4f06-b033-b4a994505bff (QA's selected account, not accounts[0]) — confirms getSelectedAccount(list) is honored. (5) REGRESSION pnl sign — a leftover 'TEST_UI_loss_sign' loss trade rendered as '−100.00 USD' (negative, in red) proving the normalize_pnl contract still holds. All 5 test trades created were cleaned up (4 via cleanup pass + 1 via test-delete). testIDs used: auth-email/password/submit, tab-journal, journal-screen, journal-add, trade-modal, trade-result-{win|loss|breakeven}, trade-pnl, trade-save, trade-<id>, trade-edit-<id>, trade-delete-<id>.
critical_code_review_comments: journal.tsx save() (line 31) correctly branches: editing → updateTrade(...) then setTrades(map replace by id); new → createTrade(...) then setTrades(prev => [created, ...prev]). No getTrades() call in the save path. Matches the perf fix intent.

journal.tsx remove() (line 32) is a textbook optimistic delete: filter locally first, then await deleteTrade(); on catch, only then do a full getTrades(account.id) refetch as fallback. Measured DOM removal within 148ms of the click — well under the 300ms perception threshold.

useFocusEffect (line 28) still refetches trades on tab focus — that's correct and expected (keeps list fresh when returning to Journal). It is NOT called after each save/delete because save/delete don't navigate.
Type safety: updateTrade returns Trade so setTrades map is safely typed. createTrade returns Trade prepended — new trade appears at top which matches backend list ordering (newest first).
Minor risk: if two rapid deletes fail (network), the fallback getTrades() will run for each — but since the current behavior is exception-only, this is rare. Not blocking.
No SafeAreaView / deprecated expo-av / expo-barcode-scanner / expo-background-fetch usage in the touched file. No React Native red screen encountered during testing.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of executed flows: login → Journal → 5 consecutive creates (0 refetch, avg 0.89s each) → in-place edit (0 refetch) → optimistic delete (DOM removal in 148ms) → cleanup. Account isolation + PnL sign regressions also pass.

rca_of_issue: Original bug: user with 49+ trades saw the app freeze during rapid save/delete because every mutation called getTrades(account.id) which fetched and re-rendered the entire list (O(N) network + O(N) rerender per action). Fix applied to /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/journal.tsx: (a) save() now uses setTrades(prev => [created, ...prev]) on create and setTrades(items.map(item => item.id===updated.id ? updated : item)) on edit — O(1) network, O(N) rerender only over the changed slice; (b) remove() filters locally first (optimistic) then awaits deleteTrade, with a getTrades() only in the catch fallback. Verified by network instrumentation that 5 POSTs + 1 PATCH + 1 DELETE produced 0 GETs. DOM-level check showed 148ms optimistic removal on delete. No regressions to account isolation or pnl sign normalization.
